articles.title: Apuestas y pronósticos Real Madrid vs Real Sociedad
articles.standfirst: Bet365 te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta a Real Madrid y Real Sociedad en el Santiago Bernabéu correspondiente a la jornada 1 de LaLiga EA Sports 26-27
articles.summary: Bet365 te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta a Real Madrid y Real Sociedad en el Santiago Bernabéu correspondiente a la jornada 1 de LaLiga EA Sports 26-27
articles.body: Real Madrid y Real Sociedad se enfrentan en el Santiago Bernabéu en uno de los partidos pendientes de la primera jornada de LaLiga EA Sports 2026-27. El conjunto blanco llega al estreno ante su afición después de comenzar la segunda etapa de Mourinho con una victoria sobre la bocina frente al Espanyol a domicilio. La Real Sociedad, por su parte, no tuvo el inicio deseado y cayó contra el Betis en su primer compromiso liguero y ahora tienen que visitar uno de los estadios más complicados del campeonato. Favorito para el partido entre Real Madrid y Real Sociedad El Real Madrid parte como claro favorito para hacerse con los tres puntos en el Bernabéu, avalado además por un historial reciente muy favorable ante el conjunto donostiarra. En los diez últimos enfrentamientos entre ambos se han producido siete victorias madridistas, dos empates y únicamente un triunfo de la Real Sociedad. Las casas de apuestas reflejan ese favoritismo con una cuota de 1.38 en Bet365 por la victoria del Real Madrid, mientras que el empate cotiza a 5.28 y el triunfo visitante se paga a 7.00. Ambos equipos marcan El Real Madrid comenzó el campeonato con un encuentro en el que consiguió marcar, pero también encajó frente al Espanyol, mientras que la Real Sociedad se quedó sin ver portería en su derrota contra el Betis. Los antecedentes directos, sin embargo, ofrecen una perspectiva algo más favorable al escenario de goles en ambas porterías, ya que esto sucedió en tres de los cinco últimos enfrentamientos entre ambos conjuntos. Con estos datos, las apuestas deportivas conceden una ligera ventaja a la opción de que ambos consigan marcar. Bet365 ofrece una cuota de 1.75 para que ambos equipos marquen y de 2.00 para que al menos uno de los dos se quede sin anotar. Primer equipo en marcar El Real Madrid ya demostró en su estreno liguero su capacidad para tomar la iniciativa y terminar imponiéndose al Espanyol, mientras que la Real Sociedad comenzó perdiendo frente al Betis. Además, el conjunto blanco consiguió adelantarse en el marcador en cuatro de los cinco últimos enfrentamientos directos contra los donostiarras, una tendencia que refuerza su condición de favorito en este mercado. Bet365 paga una cuota de 1.36 a que el Real Madrid marcará primero, 3.00 a que lo hará la Real Sociedad y 19.00 a que el encuentro finalizará sin goles. Número total de goles (Over/Under) Los dos equipos dejaron tendencias diferentes en cuanto al número de goles en su estreno liguero. En el encuentro del Real Madrid frente al Espanyol se superó la barrera de los 2.5 tantos, mientras que en el duelo de la Real Sociedad contra el Betis no se alcanzó esa cifra. Los precedentes entre ambos, sin embargo, vuelven a apuntar hacia un partido con goles, ya que en tres de los cinco últimos enfrentamientos directos se marcaron más de 2.5 tantos totales.

articles.title: Astros Owner Jim Crane Retains Joe Espada For Rest Of Season Following GM Ouster
articles.summary: Houston Astros owner Jim Crane says manager Joe Espada will remain in the role for the remainder of the season.
articles.body: A day after parting ways with general manager Dana Brown, Houston Astros owner Jim Crane addressed the move and said manager Joe Espada will remain in the role for the remainder of the season. Before opening a three-game series against the Yankees on Tuesday, the Astros moved on from Brown, whose contract was set to expire at the end of the season. The team described the decision as mutual. Houston announced senior adviser Jeff Bagwell and assistant general managers Charles Cook, Gavin Dickey and Connor Huff will take over Brown’s responsibilities, while Crane will oversee baseball operations during the transition. "There’s no good time for any of that, you know, when you let someone go," Crane said outside the Houston clubhouse. "Just out of respect for Dana, we thought that was a time that would give him a little space to regroup. He’s a great talent. He’s been in the business a long time to get settled and to get back to work somewhere else." Brown was hired in January 2023 and succeeded James Click, who was fired six days after Houston won its second World Series title. "We worked together very closely for three and a half years," Espada said. "He gave me the opportunity to be manager of this team. It was tough. It was a tough conversation, but he was grateful for the opportunity and I’m grateful for our relationship and how we grind through this together, but it was emotional. It was a lot of emotions behind our conversation." Brown helped the Astros reach a seventh straight ALCS, which they lost in seven games to the Texas Rangers. Houston lost in a wild-card series to Detroit in 2024 and last season missed the playoffs for the first time since 2016 when it finished three games behind Seattle in the AL West and lost a tiebreaker with the Tigers for final wild-card spot. "Not everybody’s been able to do it, that’s a good run," Crane said. "We hope to keep that going. We had a little hiccup last year where we didn’t make the playoffs but we’re right there. I think some few adjustments we can get back to that and some good decisions. Certainly you got to keep working on it but the expectation that I have is that we’re in the playoffs every year. It’s hard to win every year, but to get there." The Astros began this year 20-31 but were only 5 1/2 games out of first place in a weak AL West on May 20. Houston (65-66) recovered to win 40 of its next 66 games through a 6-3 win over San Diego on Aug. 7 but entered Tuesday with nine losses in 14 games, including four to the Angels and A’s, though Crane said that performance did not influence his decision to dismiss Brown. "That didn’t have anything to do with it," Crane said. "We’re focused on winning the AL, winning the division and that’s our focus but that didn’t have anything to do with it." Espada was promoted from bench coach after the 2023 season when Dusty Baker retired. He helped the Astros recover from a 12-24 start to win their seventh AL West crown in eight seasons in 2024 and began Tuesday with a 240-214 record. "I don’t know where that got mixed up, but that’s the same answer I gave since the first of the year," Crane said. "We told him we’d deal with that at the end of the season and we’ve never changed that answer all year long." Before Crane addressed reporters for nearly 10 minutes, he met with Espada. "Focus on winning today, that’s how I left that," Espada said. "My responsibility is to lead this team. We have a very important stretch of games here. So I walk out of our office ready to go." Reporting by the Associated Press.

articles.title: NFL Confidential: How League Circles Are Reacting To Players Going Back To CFB
articles.summary: Here's what people in NFL circles are telling us about the idea of players returning to college.
articles.body: Some bizarre NFL and college football history could be made soon, and not everyone's happy about it. Former Ole Miss tight end Dae'Quan Wright was on track to become the first player to play college football after being rostered by an NFL team following his release from the Cleveland Browns this week. But as he was set to join head coach Lane Kiffin at LSU, Wright and several other college athletes learned on Tuesday that the SEC would be joining the Big Ten in disallowing players who had already signed an NFL contract from playing in their conferences. Wright was among 16 former college football players who sued the NCAA for an extra year of eligibility and were granted a temporary restraining order that would allow them to play college football in 2026. That order allowed opportunistic college head coaches, like Kiffin, to explore adding players signed to NFL contracts to their rosters in recent weeks. While college head coaches and conference administrators are starting to make their feelings known on the matter, how are people around the NFL reacting to players potentially returning to play the collegiate game? Here's what we learned from some of our conversations with people around the league. Scout: NCAA Has To ‘Get Their S--- Together’ Ralph Vacchiano: The recent news that some NFL players will potentially be allowed to return to college football this season did not go over well in NFL circles. And it only added to their confusion over what is currently happening in the NCAA. "They really have to get their s--- together," one NFL scout told me. "It feels like they’re the Wild Wild West and the rules are changing every day." The recent one could be the most confusing. It was sparked by court rulings in Colorado and Louisiana that appear to allow NFL players who entered college in 2022 to return to school for a fifth year of eligibility in the NCAA. To add to the confusion, the Big Ten went against the courts and banned players from returning from the NFL. The SEC announced it opposed the rulings, but wouldn’t stand in the players’ way. It’s unclear if any other conferences will join the Big Ten and the SEC. But the courts probably haven’t had their final say on the matter yet, which is why the NFL is bracing for an even bigger mess. "All that NIL money was bad enough. It basically wiped out the talent in the later rounds of the draft because too many marginal players could afford to stay in school," the scout told me. "But now we’re going to have guys who would’ve stayed on the practice squad leaving too? We’ll spend 3-4 months investing in their growth, developing them as a player, only to watch them go back to LSU?" "It all looks bad," an NFL executive told me by text. "But we don’t know where all this is going yet. It feels like just the beginning of a really big mess." Not Everyone In The NFL Is Sounding The Alarm, Though Eric D. Williams: The situation surrounding Wright and over a dozen other players has caused some to panic about the future of college football. However, not everyone in the NFL is worried about the recent court rulings and whether this will cause more players to return to college. One NFL agent pointed out to me that what's happening this summer is likely a one-time thing due to the NCAA's new eligibility rules. "It only applies to this tiny group of players this year who made a decision prior to the rule change," the NFL agent told me. "It would never apply again because any other player in the future would make whatever decision they made after the college season based on the 5/5 rule, if it stays in effect. "So, this really isn’t a long-term issue. It’s a one-off, so the NFL won’t and shouldn’t care about these few guys who weren’t making teams to begin with. These are the only players the ruling applies to – players who under the new rules would be eligible to play college in 2026 that under the old rules would not have been eligible. That’s it. A player at the end of 2026 who has a fifth year can decide to take it or not, and if he doesn’t and goes to the NFL, why would he get his eligibility back? He made the decision to leave knowing he had a year left. No different than a true junior leaving with two years left." Players can regain their college eligibility if they terminate their pro contract and repay any pro earnings. A handful of other players in this year’s draft class could benefit from this new ruling, like Wright. However, that loophole will be closed for the 2027 draft class and beyond. What To Make Of Players Returning To CFB Williams: If players wind up returning to college after signing with NFL teams, that also begs the question about what their future draft status will be. No one seems to know what the NFL will do yet about the draft eligibility of those specific players. But an NFL scout told me league evaluators will have to reevaluate the prospects, while proposing an idea for the league on how to handle the situation. "You have to reevaluate them because they will be getting more reps to develop and grade, similar to getting reps in the UFL or CFL," a longtime NFL scout told me. "If they like them, then they should be considered as a street free agent to sign if they were previously in an NFL camp. That’s how the NFL should handle it in my eyes."

articles.title: Cancelado el FIP Silver de Ceuta: “No está el ánimo para eventos”
articles.standfirst: La situación social que atraviesa la ciudad ha llevado a la organización a suspender esta cita del calendario profesional
articles.summary: La situación social que atraviesa la ciudad ha llevado a la organización a suspender esta cita del calendario profesional
articles.body: La crisis migratoria que atraviesa Ceuta desde el pasado mes de julio ha llevado a la cancelación del FIP Silver, cita que se había celebrado durante cuatro años en la ciudad autónoma. El torneo, cuya disputa estaba prevista entre el 8 y el 13 de septiembre, finalmente no se llevará a cabo. Se trata de una medida adoptada por la Federación de Pádel de Ceuta con la conformidad de la Federación Internacional de Pádel (FIP) y de la Federación Española de Pádel (FEP). La organización ha argumentado la imposibilidad de garantizar la seguridad a través de un comunicado oficial: “Hemos intentado salvar todos los obstáculos que iban apareciendo, pero llega el momento en el que la sensatez y el sentido común deben primar para decidir esta cancelación en el momento en el que no podemos garantizar ni la seguridad ni tampoco la salud de participantes, técnicos, acompañantes, personal de organización y público que pudiera asistir al evento”. En declaraciones a MARCA, el presidente de la Federación de Pádel de Ceuta, Agustín Atencia, explicó los motivos que han conducido a esta determinación: “No era el momento idóneo. Está habiendo violaciones, también hay enfermedades como la sarna, tuberculosis… La cordura debe prevalecer por muchas ganas que tenga uno de este torneo. Es una cuestión básicamente de seguridad”. Desde la federación territorial señalan asimismo que la portavocía del gobierno local les comunicó el pasado 18 de agosto que los eventos deportivos “iban a tener muy complicado desarrollarse con normalidad”. A ello se añaden los contactos mantenidos con responsables sanitarios, políticos, militares y de las Fuerzas y Cuerpos de Seguridad del Estado quienes, según se indica en la nota oficial, informaron de que “la ciudad está al borde del colapso en varios ámbitos”, un contexto que los organizadores consideran que “no podemos ni debemos ignorar”. Más allá del análisis técnico e institucional, Atencia trasladó su valoración personal sobre el contexto actual: “Está también el corazón. Esta no es mi ciudad. Esta no es la Ceuta que le quiero enseñar yo al mundo con este torneo. Esta Ceuta no es verdad. Quiero enseñarle la Ceuta hospitalaria, quiero enseñarle la Ceuta bonita, quiero enseñarle la Ceuta que tiene un clima estupendo y que tiene una infraestructura perfecta para el turismo y para el pádel”. El dirigente ceutí lamentó las consecuencias del aplazamiento: “Los ánimos no están para eventos. Lo estamos pasando muy mal, la verdad. Lo que más se pierde no es solo lo económico o lo logístico, es ese huequito que nos habíamos ganado en el mapa internacional durante las cuatro ediciones anteriores. Ese trabajo que llevamos haciendo cinco años para que la FIP confíe en nosotros”. En sus ediciones previas, el torneo había contado con la participación de jugadores del circuito internacional como Miguel Lamperti, Leo Augsburger, Fran Guerrero o Mariano González, pasando de la categoría FIP Rise a la FIP Silver, de mayor dotación económica y puntuación. De cara al futuro, Atencia manifestó su intención de retomar la prueba en la siguiente temporada: “El año que viene volveremos con más ganas y con una edición mejor. El objetivo es que sea la mejor de la historia para olvidar este mal trago. Quiero mandar un mensaje de ánimo también. Ceuta es una ciudad resistente y nuestra sociedad está dando ejemplo”. En esta misma línea, el comunicado oficial concluye señalando que trabajarán para regresar “con más fuerza si cabe”. La federación local trasladó su agradecimiento a la FEP y a la FIP por el apoyo recibido: “Nos han dado total libertad para decidir lo que nosotros creyeramos más conveniente tanto para la prueba como para la ciudad”, confirmando su intención de solicitar de nuevo la fecha en el calendario del próximo año: “Tenemos que solicitarlo, pero te adelanto que lo vamos a hacer y creemos que nos lo van a volver a conceder como todos estos años”.

articles.title: Rockstar Games Responds to Grand Theft Auto VI Gameplay Leaks Ahead of Extended Look Trailer
articles.summary: Rockstar Games released a statement Wednesday regarding the recent gameplay leaks for the highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto VI video game.
articles.body:
Rockstar Games released a statement Wednesday regarding the recent gameplay leaks for the highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto VI video game.

In the statement, Rockstar Games noted that while it has been "heartbreaking" for the development team to see gameplay get leaked before it was ready to be shown, everyone involved is still "very excited" about the extended look, which will drop Thursday at 3 p.m. ET on Netflix:

York Responded to Ad on Prostitution Site Before Arrest

IGN's Wesley Yin-Poole reported Tuesday that 14 gameplay videos have been leaked, with the most recent ones featuring a nightclub, beach and video game store.

It has been 13 years since the release of Grand Theft Auto V, making GTA VI one of the most long-awaited video games in history.

Originally slated for a 2025 release, GTA VI was pushed back until May 26, 2026, and then again until Nov. 19, 2026.

The initial Grand Theft Auto VI trailer dropped back in December 2023, followed by a second official trailer in May 2025, offering gamers a glimpse into the next generation of one of the most popular video game franchises of all time:

While the trailers helped whet the appetites of those who have been waiting for a new entry in the Grand Theft Auto series for well over a decade, the long wait time for the game's release left Rockstar susceptible to additional leaks.

Rockstar is close to the finish line now with GTA VI being less than three months away from dropping, and Thursday was meant to be the deepest dive into the game yet.

While certain aspects of Grand Theft Auto VI have been spoiled for some gamers who decided to check out the leaks, the extended look figures to represent the most Rockstar has shown off thus far in an official capacity.

The long wait will finally be over and GTA fans will get to see what the game has to offer firsthand on Nov. 19 when Grand Theft Auto VI officially drops on the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S consoles.

articles.title: Star Wars Zero Company Review, Gameplay Impressions, Videos and Top Features
articles.summary: Star Wars Zero Company from developers Bit Reactor and Respawn Entertainment takes a familiar genre, puts a beloved franchise in the thick of it and invites players to dive deep.
articles.body:
Star Wars Zero Company from developers Bit Reactor and Respawn Entertainment takes a familiar genre, puts a beloved franchise in the thick of it and invites players to dive deep.

Comparisons to genre heavyweights like XCOM are inescapable. No accident: Names who worked on XCOM and the criminally underrated Marvel's Midnight Suns have a hand in the efforts here.

The result is an easy to pick up and play experience with some surprising depth and a Star Wars tale that is very strong in narrative and memorable characters.

York Responded to Ad on Prostitution Site Before Arrest

Zero Company has, without a doubt, the potential to be one of the best games of the year and soon have new releases being compared to it, not the other way around.

Zero Company's production values are…intense.

This is easily one of the best-looking games on the market and the authenticity to the Star Wars brand is both impressive and super immersive.

It has all the bells and whistles, really. The powerhouse graphics look great, the sound design is splendid, the ambiance and overall soundtrack is exactly what it needs to be for the brand and the overall package is exactly what one would dream up when thinking about a Star Wars themed XCOM.

Indeed, Zero Company isn't trying to duck comparisons with its gameplay. Rather, it's trying to layer atop the tried-and-true stuff.

The cover system is there. Full cover is a 50 percent penalty. Flanking leads to exposure states. Certain cover can be destroyed. There's an overwatch system to make characters auto-shoot opponents that enter the zone. Action points per turn govern, well, actions.

And yes, the hallmark of the genre, missing on a shot that has a 90 percent chance to hit? It's there.

Interesting layerings on the formula include being able to call for backup once per turn, assisting attacks. There are ultimate abilities, too, charged through an "advantage" point system shared by all friendly characters that increases by attacking enemies.

These ultimate abilities range from massive things like a rocket launcher attack to less costly, little strategy nuance, such as the ability to refresh a squadmate's AP for that turn.

Different primary weapons define each type of character capable of being added to squads.

Each character, too can equip a certain amount of utilities, talents and specializations.

Specializations won't shock those familiar with XCOM games and similar. Characters can go full-blown assault, the tank-like heavy class, medic, and so on.

Speaking of character and squad makeup, there are stakes. Characters getting defeated rack up injuries. A third injury means permadeath for a character, so players must carefully manage things not just in battle, but post-and-pre battle, too. Except for the main character, anyway, that just leads to a game-over.

Impressive depth and teambuilding strategies here too, no doubt. There's no restriction on pairing certain primary weapons with certain specializations. Weapons being moddable, too, is one of the many things that will lead to unique player-to-player builds that can change for a variety of different encounters.

Mission structures get a nice mixup too. Side missions are standard things like rescue missions or hold-the-area waves. But story missions can have multiple stages with some exploration and storytelling phases to break up the action.

Zero Company hits on some of the best story beats and characters the Star Wars universe has offered in years.

Players assume the role of Hawks, the leader of the game's namesake, "Zero Company." There's a rebellious nature to it all, and baddies to fight and the narrative does a good job of looping in the many different types of enemies and characters documented in a way that makes sense.

Beyond the narrative, managing the "Den" is similar to a variety of games. There's always a ton to do, to the point it might turn some players away because they just want to get back into the fights. Others, though, will appreciate the depth and the sense of immersion it provides in terms of really feeling in command of a multi-layered organization.

The hub does some of the basic stuff players would expect. Players can recruit new members and outfit their squads, among other things.

There are little side missions too that can be largely text-based. It's immersive to pop into the operations center and make key strategic decisions for in-progress, off-screen missions, even if they're simple text-based experiences.

Perhaps a refreshing twist on the concept, at least for similar strategy games, is being able to put boots on the ground and go around talking to characters. It's a fun wrinkle similar to old Star Wars classics like Knights of the OId Republic, which can help players care about the characters they're sending into battle more than usual.

Along the way, Zero Company runs well and has the expected suite of options within the solid UI.

Zero Company sort of snuck up on the gaming calendar this year. A tactical RPG in the XCOM mold with Star Wars window dressing was a little easy to overlook.

There's a great Star Wars tale here and the combination of the source material and genre is a no-brainer in a way Gears War Tactics or Midnight Suns were years ago. The gameplay is a chef's kiss balance between pick-up-and-play approachable and where-did-the-hours-go strategic.

Not bad for Zero Company, really, a bit of an underdog story that now lands as a serious Game of the Year contender.

articles.title: Emiliano Martinez transfer news: Chelsea considering late move for Aston Villa and Argentina goalkeeper
articles.summary: Emiliano Martinez needs to find a new club after Aston Villa signed Zion Suzuki from Parma for nearly £30m; Chelsea's current No 1 goalkeeper Robert Sanchez came under criticism after two errors in Monday's win at Fulham; Martinez was wanted by Juventus but that deal fell through
articles.body:
The Argentina international's representatives have offered Martinez to Chelsea.

Chelsea's current No 1 goalkeeper Robert Sanchez came under criticism after his error in Monday's win at Fulham.

Martinez needs to find a new club after Villa signed Zion Suzuki from Parma for nearly £30m.

Argentina's World Cup-winning goalkeeper was the subject of interest from Juventus but they chose to sign Guglielmo Vicario from Spurs.
